title: Zone hunt & forging
summary: Find new rewards, socket heroic augments and forge the next quality.
body:
Live testing: The base Spell Damage and Healing Amount caps are now 750. Earned Hunt headroom remains additive. Hunt rewards, drop chances, tasks and forging costs are unchanged.

Forty-eight enabled Classic combat zones offer a new augment family and an equipment family. The release is installed for live testing. Explore the zone directory or item index.

How drops work

Each eligible native enemy has two independent rolls: 0.5% for its zone augment and 0.5% for its zone equipment. Both may drop together. Ordinary loot remains. Each family averages one reward per 200 eligible kills, with no guarantee or pity counter.

Quality after a successful family roll
QualityChance
Base60%
Polished30%
Exalted8%
Ascension2%

Only approved native enemies qualify. Cities, hubs, merchants, pets and summoned copies do not. Kithicor requires eligible nighttime undead.

Sockets & heroic stats

Eligible head, arms, hands, chest, legs and feet armor has a type-22 socket for these augments. Existing sockets remain. Required levels and compatibility still apply.

At level 50, every two effective heroic INT from these socketed augments adds one point to the item Spell Damage cap, up to +30. Heroic WIS does the same for Healing Amount. With the current base cap of 750, either can reach 780. Increasing a cap does not grant the underlying bonus; you still need enough actual Spell Damage or Healing Amount equipped.

Forge matching rewards into the next quality

  1. Carry three identical Base rewards, or four identical Polished or Exalted rewards, unequipped and unmodified.
  2. Leave combat, empty your cursor, and close loot, trade and merchant windows.
  3. Type #zoneforge and choose the named upgrade.

3 Base → 1 Polished; 4 Polished → 1 Exalted; 4 Exalted → 1 Ascension. There is no fee or random failure. Different zones and qualities cannot mix. An item's built-in color is allowed; a different player-applied dye color is not. Socketed, player-dyed, ornamented, customized or evolving items cannot be inputs. Ascension is the final quality.

For Polished and Exalted rewards, Artisan Veyra’s Reforging Box offers the same four-copy upgrades. The box also supports eligible ordinary tiered gear. The box also accepts three identical Base copies for Polished.

Trading & resale

These rewards can be traded between players but have no merchant resale value. If an upgrade result is unclear or items appear missing, stop retrying and tell the owner what happened.

The Vigil of the Dawn — live testing

Chapterhouse adds Ember of the First Dawn, a level-50 type-22 armor augment with four qualities. It follows existing Hunt headroom and zone forging. Its curated static enemies have a 0.5% augment roll; summoned encounter shades do not. Read the quest guide and reward catalog.

The Ashen Compact — live testing

The Ashen Compact is an installed level-50 Shadow Knight helmet campaign in a curated Kael expedition. Its paired server and client release is available for testing; full encounter, rendering and balance acceptance remain open.

Cinder of the Ashen Compact is a separate type-22 STA/INT augment family, with the existing 0.5% static-enemy roll and 60/30/8/2 quality weights. The ordinary 48-zone Hunt pools are unchanged.

Hate rewards across both layouts

The new private Hate layout uses the original Plane of Hate Hunt family, approved enemy list and drop chances. The catalog’s hateplane rewards apply to both layouts; this update does not add a second Hunt family or change forging. Dungeon entry and testing.

Broader zone augments — Not released

The prepared update lets all regular spawned combat enemies roll their zone augment in public zones and Grind/Raid instances, including low-level and named enemies. The augment rate stays 0.5%, with the same 60/30/8/2 qualities. Pets, service NPCs, protected or invisible actors, temporary encounter adds and restored corpses are excluded. Wearable Hunt rewards keep their existing eligible-enemy, level and night rules. Hate B gains its existing Blackspire Prism family; its own equipment family stays disabled, while managed Grind/Raid retains original Hate’s equipment drops. This is a preview, not current live behavior.
